nodes.description: Reported alleles are an exon 7 donor splice-site variant causing skipping of exons 6 and 7, two nonsense variants (p.Tyr316Ter as summarized by panel curation, and c.551G>A p.Trp184Ter) and a frameshift (c.1288delT, p.Cys430fs), all homozygous. The splice and frameshift alleles were shown to reduce or abolish CAP2 protein in patient cells; the nonsense alleles are predicted loss of function.

nodes.description: Homozygous gene-trap mice have reduced body weight and survival, dilated cardiomyopathy, sarcomere disarray, fibrosis, reduced myofibrillar calcium cooperativity, bradycardia, conduction delay, connexin43 maldistribution and inducible ventricular arrhythmias.

Knockout males show reduced survival, small size, microphthalmia, cardiac conduction disease and, after six months, dilated cardiomyopathy; females are much less affected. Knockout hearts show MRTFB nuclear accumulation and SRF target activation. The alpha-actin isoform findings (PMID:33742108) come from a separate EUCOMM Cap2 tm1a knockout colony, not the line described in PMID:26616005.

nodes.description: Cap2 mutant mice have slowed atrial, atrioventricular and infra-Hisian conduction, abnormal connexin43 distribution and inducible ventricular arrhythmias. Cardiomyocyte-specific knockout mice died suddenly of complete heart block, showing that the conduction defect is cardiomyocyte-autonomous. In patients, first-degree atrioventricular block, intraventricular conduction delay and ventricular premature complexes were documented in one child, and the founding report describes conduction disease, naming supraventricular tachycardia in its title only.

nodes.description: In Cap2 knockout mice and cultured knockout cardiomyocytes, cardiac alpha-actin is partly replaced by smooth-muscle and skeletal alpha-actin in thin filaments, myofibrils remain immature and disorganized, and cardiomyocytes are smaller and rounder. nodes.description: Cap2 knockout hearts show nuclear accumulation of MRTFB and activation of SRF-dependent and fetal genes such as Myl9, Acta2 and Nppa before overt cardiac disease. An SRF inhibitor reduced these targets and delayed disease in cardiomyocyte-specific knockout mice, supporting a contributory rather than initiating role. In mouse embryonic fibroblasts, CAP2 loss instead reduces basal nuclear MRTF-A and SRF activity, so the direction of the effect depends on cell type. This has not been measured in patients. GO:0045944 is bound because GO has no SRF-specific process term.
